sections.h2: How do Rome owners usually sell a house in a hurry?
sections.html:
A Rome owner can hire a realtor, go it alone, or let a cash buyer take the house as it is. Each has a place. The winner depends on the house's age, its repair list, and whether a tenant or a co-heir also has a say.

Rome has a large rental share, which affects how houses change hands. Owners live in 49.2% of Rome's homes, so about half of the housing is rented. A plain cash sale tends to suit landlords, heirs of a family house and owners of an older home better than a long listing does.

  • Cash buyer: one walk-through, an offer soon after, no repair work and a closing day that suits you.
  • Realtor sale: the best shot at full market value for a house in good order, at the cost of showings, an inspection and a lender's calendar.
  • Private sale: no commission, but you carry the pricing, the contract and every buyer question.

Total what each route would leave you after fees, repairs, and the months of taxes, insurance and utilities you cover while waiting.

sections.h2: Where is Rome, Georgia, and how did it grow?
sections.html:
Rome is the seat of Floyd County in northwest Georgia, sitting where the Etowah and Oostanaula rivers join to form the Coosa. The New Georgia Encyclopedia places it inside a triangle formed by Atlanta, Birmingham and Chattanooga and says the city was founded in 1834 on the site of a large Cherokee settlement called Head of Coosa.

Transportation and cotton drove the early economy. Steamboats reached Rome in 1836, a railroad charter followed in 1839, and Norfolk Southern still runs a freight yard in the city. The Clocktower was built in 1871, Cherokee Baptist Female College, later Shorter University, opened in 1873, and Berry College was founded in 1902 on the north edge of the city.

Textiles and carpet shaped the twentieth century, and the encyclopedia reports that both have largely faded. General Electric and Georgia Power's Plant Hammond arrived in the 1950s. The encyclopedia says health care and education carry more weight than the older industries, listing three hospitals, two public colleges and two private ones, along with manufacturers such as Suzuki Manufacturing of America and the North American headquarters of Pirelli Tire. Rome and Floyd County were designated one of Georgia's metropolitan statistical areas in 2003.

Downtown is part of that story. When major retailers left for malls, the encyclopedia says remaining owners formed a downtown development authority and an organization called PRIDE, Rome became one of Georgia's early Main Street cities, and the National Trust for Historic Preservation gave downtown a Great American Main Street Award in 2003. A house within reach of Broad Street sits in a part of town with a long record of public reinvestment, and sellers can mention that when a buyer asks about the area.

sections.h2: What do Census figures say about Rome homes and incomes?
sections.html:
QuickFacts has Rome at 38,934 residents in mid-2025, against 37,713 at the 2020 census and 36,303 in 2010. Growth since the April 2020 estimates base is 2.7%, far below the 24.8% shown for Perry and 28.0% for Pooler over the same stretch.

  • Tenure and value: owners occupy 49.2% of homes, and the middle owner's home is worth $234,300 (2020-2024).
  • Monthly costs: owners with a mortgage pay a middle figure of $1,526, and renters $1,032.
  • Households and size: 14,983 households spread over 31.68 square miles of land.

A median household income of $54,435 in 2024 dollars gives a sense of local affordability. Health care and social assistance is the largest receipts line in QuickFacts for 2022, at $1,596,086 thousand, which fits the encyclopedia's description of Rome as a regional medical center.

sections.h2: What do Rome and Floyd County rules mean for a house sale?
sections.html:
Rome and Floyd County share a Unified Land Development Code, and the city lists it with a 2040 Comprehensive Plan on its Board of Adjustments page. Planning staff take appointments for questions about a property, a project or a request.

Requests that go to the Board of Adjustments include appeals of an administrator's decision, special exceptions, hardship variances and flood protection variances. Its third-Thursday meetings start at 2:30 in the upstairs Commission Chambers at City Hall, 601 Broad Street. An application must arrive by 5:00 p.m. on the 25th, and the earliest hearing is two months after that date.

  • Special exceptions: relief from setbacks, building height, lot width, street frontage, buffers, signs and parking requirements.
  • Hardship variances: granted only for extraordinary property conditions such as size, shape or topography, or for unnecessary hardship, and never for a condition the applicant created, a use the zoning does not allow, or added dwelling units.
  • Waiting period: after a denial, a request for the same property cannot return for 12 months unless the board shortens the wait.

If your house has a nonconforming addition, a garage apartment or a setback problem, raise it with planning staff before a buyer's survey does. A cash buyer can live with the problem, and a lender may not.

sections.h2: How do I appeal a Floyd County assessment on a Rome house?
sections.html:
Floyd County wants a letter to its Board of Assessors, mailed within 45 days of the date on the assessment notice. Allowed grounds are taxability, uniformity, value, or a denied homestead exemption.

Assessors and appraisal staff review the file and may raise, lower or keep the figure. A figure that stays goes straight on to the Board of Equalization. A figure that changes gives the owner 21 days to contest it in writing. The county describes four formal routes, summarized below.

RouteGrounds allowedKey timing from the county
Board of EqualizationAny groundsWritten appeal inside 45 days; its decision can go to Superior Court within 30 days
Hearing OfficerValue or uniformity only; non-homesteaded parcel valued over $1 millionCounty has 90 days to review
Binding arbitrationValue onlyTaxpayer has 45 days after the county's acknowledgment to submit a certified appraisal
Superior CourtAny groundsAppeal within 45 days of the notice; fees apply

Source: Floyd County Board of Assessors, Appeals page.

sections.h2: What is recorded when a Rome sale closes?
sections.html:
Before a Rome deed can be recorded, the state transfer tax has to be paid. The clerks' cooperative that runs the PT-61 portal calls it an excise tax on real property sales, and the filer prints one PT-61 to go with the deed.

In Rome, recording happens at the Floyd County clerk's office. Have your settlement agent say who owes the tax under your contract and which rate fits your deed.

sections.h2: When does a cash sale fit a Rome house?
sections.html:
Cash is worth pricing out in these Rome situations:

  • A landlord selling a rental with tenants in place, or one scarred by a departing tenant.
  • A family house near downtown that needs a roof, wiring or foundation work.
  • An estate in which heirs live in different states and cannot manage repairs.
  • A seller with a mortgage in arrears who needs a closing date before the lender's deadline.

Ask for a written offer, an explanation of who pays closing costs and a closing date. Then compare it with a listing's likely net.

faqs.q: Is Rome, Georgia, a renter-heavy market?
faqs.a: Yes. Owners occupy 49.2% of homes in the 2020-2024 figures, so about half the housing is rented. That shapes who buys and who sells.

faqs.q: What is the window for contesting a Floyd County value?
faqs.a: Forty-five days, counted from the date the notice was mailed, by letter to the Board of Assessors. A changed value opens a further 21 days to contest the new figure.

faqs.q: Who handles variance requests in Rome?
faqs.a: The joint Rome and Floyd County Board of Adjustments. It sits on third Thursdays at City Hall and wants applications by the 25th of the month. Planning staff will book a time to talk through your request.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Rome house that has code or permit problems?
faqs.a: Yes, though you should disclose it. A cash buyer can take the house as it stands, and a lender may insist on a fix first. Planning staff can tell you what the city's file shows for the address.

faqs.q: Which papers record a Rome deed?
faqs.a: Floyd County's clerk receives the deed together with a PT-61 form, after the transfer tax is paid. You complete the form online, and the settlement agent typically files it.
